name: 10K in 10 weeks
description: For runners who already cover 5 km. Four runs a week up to a finished 10K.
guide:
Entry requirement: run 5 km non-stop, reasonably comfortably. If you're not there yet, do the 5K program first.

Four runs a week: intervals on Tuesday, an easy run on Wednesday, tempo on Thursday and the long run on Saturday. Monday, Friday and Sunday are rest. That layout keeps a day between the two hard sessions and never puts the long run straight after one.

80 % of the mileage goes slow. This is the most common mistake: running the easy days too fast leaves you with no legs on the days that matter.

Down weeks lower the load on purpose. Don't skip them or move them forward — that's when the body absorbs the work.

If you miss a week, restart at the week before the one you were due, not where you left off. If you miss three or more, go back to the start of the block.

Effort guide (RPE): 3-4 you can hold a conversation; 7 you speak in three- or four-word bursts; 8-9 single words only.

weeks.title: Getting going
weeks.goal: Get used to four runs a week.

days.title: Monday — Rest
days.notes: Full rest. Walking and stretching are fine.

days.title: Tuesday — Intervals, 6 × 400 m
days.notes: Every rep at the same pace. If the last one drops more than 10 s, you started too fast.

exercises.name: 60 m strides
exercises.notes: Build up to interval pace and let go. This is not a sprint.

exercises.name: 400 m repeats
exercises.notes: Fast but controlled: you could do one more rep at the end.

exercises.name: Very easy jog
exercises.notes: Bring the heart rate down before you stop; don't cut it dead.

days.title: Wednesday — Easy run, 5 km
days.notes: The easy day has to be genuinely easy. This is where the endurance is built.

exercises.name: Ankle and hip mobility
exercises.notes: Ankle circles, knee lifts, heel kicks.

exercises.name: Continuous easy run
exercises.notes: Full-conversation pace.

exercises.name: Stretching
exercises.notes: Calf, hamstring, quad and glute. No bouncing.

days.title: Thursday — Tempo, 15 min
days.notes: Comfortably hard: three or four words at a time, no more.

exercises.name: 60 m strides
exercises.notes: Build up to interval pace and let go. This is not a sprint.

exercises.name: Tempo effort
exercises.notes: A pace you could hold for an hour if someone made you.

exercises.name: Very easy jog
exercises.notes: Bring the heart rate down before you stop; don't cut it dead.

days.title: Friday — Rest
days.notes: Full rest. Walking and stretching are fine.

days.title: Saturday — Long run, 6 km
days.notes: The most important session of the week. It goes slow — slower than the easy run.

exercises.name: Ankle and hip mobility
exercises.notes: Ankle circles, knee lifts, heel kicks.

exercises.name: Long run
exercises.notes: Drink if it runs past 60 min. Finishing whole beats finishing fast.

exercises.name: Stretching
exercises.notes: Calf, hamstring, quad and glute. No bouncing.

days.title: Sunday — Rest
days.notes: Full rest. Walking and stretching are fine.
